derinde.explanation: "Derinde" means "in there". It is built from "der" (there) and "inde" (inside). To say where someone is in another room: "Katten er derinde" (The cat is in there). For the room you are in, use "herinde" (in here): "Jeg er herinde" (I am in here).

dermed.explanation: "Dermed" means "with that". It is built from "der" (there) and "med" (with). To say what follows from something you just did: "Han skrev under, og dermed er aftalen indgået" (He signed, and with that the deal is made).

dernede.explanation: "Dernede" means "down there". To say where something is in a lower place: "Katten er dernede" (The cat is down there). For a higher place, use "deroppe" (up there): "Katten er deroppe" (The cat is up there).

dernæst.explanation: "Dernæst" means "next". To list steps in order, say it after "først" (first): "Først kommer maden, dernæst kommer kaffen" (First comes the food, next comes the coffee).

deroppe.explanation: "Deroppe" means "up there". To say where something is in a higher place: "Vores lejlighed ligger deroppe" (Our apartment is up there). For the place where you are, use "heroppe" (up here): "Heroppe er der koldt" (It is cold up here).

derovre.explanation: "Derovre" means "over there". To point to a place at a distance: "Bogen ligger derovre" (The book is over there). To say you go there, use "derover" (over there, with movement): "Jeg går derover" (I am going over there).

derude.explanation: "Derude" means "out there". To say where children are outside: "Børnene er derude" (The children are out there). For inside something, use "derinde" (in there): "Børnene er derinde" (The children are in there).

derudover.explanation: "Derudover" means "in addition". At the start of a sentence, the verb follows right after it: "Derudover er prisen lav" (In addition, the price is low).

design.explanation: "Design" means "design". It is an et-word, as "designet" (the design) shows. To say what field someone works in: "Hun arbejder med design" (She works in design). Danish furniture and lamps are known abroad as "dansk design" (Danish design).

desperat.explanation: "Desperat" means "desperate". To say what a person is desperate to get, use "efter" (for): "Hun er desperat efter et job" (She is desperate for a job).

desuden.explanation: "Desuden" means "besides". To add one more point after a reason: "Huset er for dyrt. Desuden ligger det langt væk." (The house is too expensive. Besides, it is far away.)

desværre.explanation: "Desværre" means "unfortunately". To tell someone bad news: "Desværre er butikken lukket" (Unfortunately the shop is closed).

det.explanation: "Det" means "it". It stands for a thing that takes "et": "Jeg har et hus, og det er stort" (I have a house, and it is big). Things that take "en" use "den": "Jeg har en bil, og den er stor" (I have a car, and it is big). When you point to something just said or done, it means "that": "Det er sjovt" (That is fun). When there is no particular thing, such as weather: "Det regner" (It is raining).

det er.explanation: "Det er" means "it is". To name or describe a thing: "Det er en bog" (It is a book). To point at someone and say who they are, it means "that is": "Det er min bror" (That is my brother).

det er en god idé.explanation: "Det er en god idé" means "That's a good idea". To agree with a suggestion: "Skal vi gå en tur?" "Det er en god idé." (Shall we go for a walk? That's a good idea.) The short form is "God idé!" (Good idea!).

det er hip som hap.explanation: "Det er hip som hap" means "It's all the same". To say you do not mind which option is chosen: "Kaffe eller te?" "Det er hip som hap." (Coffee or tea? Either is fine.)

det er i orden.explanation: "Det er i orden" means "It's okay". To agree to a plan: "Vi ses klokken otte?" "Det er i orden." (See you at eight? That's fine.) Literally, "i orden" means "in order".

det er ikke så svært.explanation: "Det er ikke så svært" means "It's not that hard". It is built from "svært" (difficult) and "ikke så" (not so). To reassure someone who is stuck: "Jeg kan ikke finde ud af det." "Det er ikke så svært." (I cannot figure it out. It's not that hard.)

det er lige det.explanation: "Det er lige det" means "Yes, that's exactly it". To confirm that someone has understood you: "Du mener, at vi skal vente?" "Det er lige det." (You mean we should wait? That's exactly it.) Said short, "lige det" means "exactly that": "Jeg ville have lige det" (I wanted exactly that).

det er lige meget.explanation: "Det er lige meget" means "It doesn't matter". To say you do not mind which option is chosen: "Pizza eller pasta?" "Det er lige meget." (Pizza or pasta? It doesn't matter.) To say "I don't care", add "mig" (me): "Det er mig lige meget". This can sound rude.

det er min skyld.explanation: "Det er min skyld" means "It's my fault". To blame someone else, change "min" (my) to "hans" (his): "Det er hans skyld" (It's his fault).

det er rigtigt.explanation: "Det er rigtigt" means "That's right". To agree that something is correct: "Er mødet klokken ti?" "Ja, det er rigtigt." (Is the meeting at ten? Yes, that's right.) A mix-up: "rigtig" before another word means "really", as in "rigtig godt" (really good).

det er synd.explanation: "Det er synd" means "That's a shame". To answer bad news: "Hun er syg i dag." "Åh, det er synd." (She is sick today. Oh, that's a shame.) To name the person you feel sorry for, add "for" (for): "Det er synd for dig" (That's too bad for you).
